summary: Auth regression + core-flow smoke after iteration 5 (frontend-polish-only). 12/12 pytest cases pass on the public preview URL. Reproduced the user bug 'Sign in not working' and could NOT reproduce it against the OptiScreen backend: POST /api/auth/login with seeded credentials (trader@optiscreen.app / TestPass123!) returns 200 with a valid session_token and a user object showing plan='advance', questionnaire_complete=true, consent_signed=true, no _id or password leak. Wrong password and unknown email both correctly return 401 {detail:'Invalid credentials'}. GET /api/auth/me with the Bearer session_token returns the same user (user_id matches); 401 without the header and 401 with a bad token. POST /api/auth/register with the existing seed email returns 400 ('Email already registered'). Regression on core flows (no backend changes expected): POST /api/screener/ticker-options {AAPL, month} returns {result:{strategy, legs (each with theo_price + delta/gamma/theta/vega), premium_net, breakevens (list), max_profit, max_loss (nullable), greeks aggregate, scenario_matrix (list of {days_elapsed, pnl})}}; watchlist add+list+delete works and items are free of _id/user_id; alerts add+list+delete works and the returned object has NO _id and NO user_id (only alert_id); /api/learn/cards is public and returns 8 cards (>=6) each with id/category/title/summary. User-reported bug is confirmed NOT a backend bug — most likely Expo Go's own sign-in screen as noted by main agent.
action_items: Mark the user-reported 'Sign in not working' bug as 'not a backend bug' — the OptiScreen /api/auth/login endpoint accepts the seeded credentials end-to-end (verified via public preview URL). Most likely the user was on Expo Go's own login screen as suspected.
(Optional, pre-existing) server.py:94-100 AlertAddReq still does not validate that price_above/price_below alerts carry a numeric threshold. Low priority; carried over from iteration 4.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:299-307 /auth/login — correctly uses verify_pw against stored hash, lowercases email, pops password before returning; returns 401 on both unknown email and bad password (uniform error, no user enumeration). Good.
server.py:277-297 /auth/register — checks for duplicate email with 400, stores lowercased email, hashes password, creates session on success. Clean.
server.py:356-359 /auth/me — relies on get_user_from_token which raises 401 for both missing and invalid Bearer tokens; the user object returned excludes password and _id via projection. Good.
server.py:452-477 /screener/ticker-options — wraps enriched payload in {result: opt}; AI calls (claude) are tolerated with safe defaults if LLM fails (ai.get(...) with fallback strings).

rca_of_issue: User reported 'Sign in not working with the given email and password'. Reproduction attempt against POST /api/auth/login with the seeded credentials returned 200 OK with a valid session_token and the fully-onboarded user object. Wrong password and unknown email both return the correct 401. No backend bug exists. Root cause of the user-facing confusion was most likely the Expo Go/Expo.dev own account sign-in screen that appears before the preview loads, not the OptiScreen app's own login screen — consistent with main agent's investigation note. Mitigation: no code change required for backend; frontend-side guidance (e.g. clearer onboarding to the OptiScreen login screen within Expo Go) is a UX improvement for a future iteration.
